newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S MARACANA SOCCER TEMPLE GOES PRIVATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRAZIL'S MARACANA SOCCER TEMPLE GOES PRIVATE.

text.p: The world famous Maracana stadium in Rio de Janeiro is to come under private administration in a bid to restore the crumbling temple of Brazilian soccer to renewed glory.
The rules of the game to acquire the 30-year concession to run and refurbish the world's largest soccer stadium with a capacity of 125,000 spectators were published on Wednesday.
When the stadium was finished in 1950, its design was hailed as being years ahead of its time, but 46 years later the paint is peeling, cats roam at will and water leaks onto the terraces.

Interested investors will have to prove their financial mettle. They must possess capital of at least 46.5 million reais ($45 million) and invest 40-50 million reais ($39-49 million) in the first three years to modernise the stadium.
Maracana's decline really took off in the early 1990s when the state government of Rio de Janeiro, which owns the stadium, stopped doing even the most basic maintenance.

The state has been running Maracana at a deficit, spending around 10 million reais ($9.7 million) a year but taking in only around 5-6 million reais ($4.8-5.8 million) in receipts, said Raul Raposo, the president of the Rio de Janeiro state sports department.
"With these measures (privatization) we hope ... to restore the complex to the conditions set by FIFA and the International Olympic Committee," Raposo said.

Whoever buys Maracana will have to fit electronic scoreboards, introduce computerized ticketing and install numbered seating, Raposo said. They will also be responsible for security within the grounds.

The stadium's fall from grace was highlighted four years ago when part of the fence at the front of the upper tier collapsed and dozens of people plunged five yards (meters) onto the seating below. More than 50 people were injured and one soccer fan died as a result of his injuries.
Only 18 months earlier the Maracana grounds had been closed for several weeks after radio reporters claimed the upper tier was vibrating during a game.

Bids for the Maracana complex, which also includes the Maracanazinho gymnasium, the Celio Barros athletics stadium and the Julio de Lamare swimming complex, have to be handed in by Jan. 21. The new administrators of the stadium will have to pay the state of Rio at least 500,000 reais ($485,437) annually for the concession.
